name: fail-closed-schema-digest-approval
description: V0 campaign-controller schema pattern: rejectUnknownKeys everywhere, approval digest over canonical JSON (recursively key-sorted) so binding is key-order-independent, timestamps normalized to ISO UTC before digesting, validation clock injected via nowMs for deterministic tests, committed data profiles validated against a FixedClock pinned near fetchedAt

name: admission-boundary
description: Admission boundary pattern (warren-a252): import keys campaigns by canonical manifest digest; approveCampaign re-states the exact digest+approver; admitWorkItem runs all invariants fail-closed (expiry, policy freshness+digest, ordered membership, upstream allowlist, mutation flags, warren identity, campaign+daily budget, concurrency, one active attempt) and only then reserves per-run budget in one store.transaction. Refusals are AdmissionRefusal with a stable invariant discriminator; untrusted issue text can only cause refusals; no client import so no network can precede admission.

name: openclaw-v0-e2e-acceptance
description: The OpenClaw V0 e2e acceptance scenario (extensions/campaign-controller/src/acceptance/openclaw-v0.e2e.test.ts) proves the full fake-server vertical slice: committed profiles import, one dispatch, PR-intent render, duplicated/reordered page ingestion, controller+Warren restart, and stable single state. Dry-run no-mutation is a structural property: assert recorded fake-GitHub methods are GET/HEAD and no token reaches durable payloads. Operator boundary published in extensions/campaign-controller/RUNBOOK.md.

title: Phase 3: response loop via ephemeral follow-up runs on the PR branch; all repo behavior as profile data
rationale: Long-lived/extended-TTL run pods were rejected: they idle-burn budget and fight the ephemeral-run model. Fresh journaled follow-up runs dispatched onto the existing PR head branch give the same result with bounded, per-intent-auditable cost. Repo-agnosticism is the exit hatch if openclaw proves too costly a target.

name: phase3-mutation-flags
description: Phase-3 mutations (warren-094b) extend the enforced-by-absence pattern per flag: one transport class per mutation, constructible only from a policy with that individual flag true, intents verified against policy upstream coordinates, journaling via shared executeJournaledMutation (planned-before-I/O, canonical digest, pr_execute-identical transitions). Extending EXECUTABLE_MUTATION_FLAGS is the reviewable schema event; widening MUTATION_FLAGS requires touching profile JSON + test policy literals because fixtures bind every flag explicitly.

name: amendment-flow-in-place
description: Manifest amendments (warren-35c4) apply IN PLACE on the campaign row rather than creating a new digest row: amendment document references campaignId + baseManifestDigest, carries only appendIssues/budget/prompt/maxConcurrentRuns/expiresAt, and its own approval envelope becomes the new manifest's approval envelope; validateCampaignManifest is re-run over the composed manifest so all invariants (digest binding, cap layering, expiry) hold for free. No superseded attention row is emitted. Planned never-executed actions are invalidated (permanent_failure/policy_violation, reservation released); executing ones stay with the dispatcher. Note: check:dups scans extensions/campaign-controller/src too — keep CLI command functions thin by extracting shared helpers.

name: pr-body-contract-as-profile-data
description: PR-body contract is profile data (warren-e361): prBodyContract on RepositoryPolicy (optional field, null keeps old profiles valid) with keyed ordered sections + disclosure/footer templates using named placeholders; intender renders via src/pr-intent/pr-body.ts walking the contract and declares no headings; profiles without a contract fall back to profiles/default.pr-body-contract.json. A guard test (src/pr-intent/pr-body.test.ts) greps extension src/ for rendered heading/template literals outside profiles/ and __golden__ fixtures, so headings must never be re-hardcoded.

name: evidence-tier-known-gap-rendering
description: Evidence tiers (warren-4dc1): the PR-body known-gap slot is a contract section key (knownGap) rendered conditionally - the renderer skips empty blocks so local-provable bodies stay byte-identical to the pre-tier goldens. Manifest tier tags bind into the approval digest; tier-vs-profile membership is cross-checked at import, not at manifest validation, because the manifest schema is profile-independent.

name: body-refresh-mutation
description: Body-refresh mutation (warren-09d2): refresh renders the ENTIRE PR body from controller-owned facts through the profile contract (responseSummary optional section key added to PR_BODY_SECTION_KEYS, default contract bumped to v3) — never patch region text. Journaled via journalMutationIntent under a key derived from renderedBodyDigest(body)=sha256(canonicalJson({body})), so same-facts re-drives replan/already_settled and changed facts are new logical effects. Divergence gate: PR snapshot now carries body; compare renderedBodyDigest(live) vs last rendered body, raise pr_body_diverged attention once, refuse unless operatorOverride. Store holds one active attempt per work item, so a second refresh intent cannot journal while the first is pending.

name: terminal-accounting-outcome
description: Terminal accounting (warren-7cd1): outcome lives as a column pair (outcome, outcome_at_ms) on work_items via migration 002, written only through recordWorkItemOutcome which is exactly-once (first recorded outcome wins over later contradicting observations). Campaign report is purely store-derived in src/report/report.ts so historical campaigns report identically after restart.

content: Validators that reuse isValidOwner must strip the suffix and validate the inner account name, otherwise profile data that exact-matches the API literal can never validate (warren-442e). extensions/campaign-controller/src/reconcile/bot-grammar.ts accepts '<owner>[bot]'; the classifier comparison stays exact-match either way.

The campaign-controller reconciler's target.botGrammar is optional, so an unwired dep degrades to a silent classifier no-op. Config sources follow the extension pattern: named CAMPAIGN_* env vars with matching flags in src/cli/config.ts; the tick command validates optional files fail-loud at startup (readJsonFile -> ConfigError on bad path, validateBotGrammar -> ValidationError on bad content) before any IO. tick.test.ts e2e tests are the proof pattern: harness({botGrammar}) with a seeded bot comment asserts github_reconcile detail.feedbackCreated > 0 and a review_bot_findings row; absent grammar asserts feedbackCreated === 0.

name: crewai-target-empirics
description: crewAI (crewAIInc/crewAI) campaign-target empirics (2026-08-31): AI-PRs are first-class — CONTRIBUTING requires only the llm-generated label (cross-fork authors cannot apply labels; ask maintainers in the PR body). Review bots: coderabbitai[bot] posts actionable findings as NEW inline review comments (italic header line + bold title — grammar observed on PR 7148), so warren-b990 edit-blindness does not bite; walkthrough comment IS edited in place. Cursor Bugbot rides as a check. Queue saturation: ~710 open PRs, and every unassigned open bug has a competing open PR (issue+PR pairs); fresh issues attract 3 PRs within a day (#7129). Candidate selection needs fast-poll or stale-competitor strategy, not backlog mining.

name: campaign-go-live-pipeline
description: Full campaign go-live on a new repo (proven on crewAI 2026-08-31, ~3h zero-to-upstream-PR): (1) profile PR merged; (2) fork via pod-held bot token (kubectl exec bun fetch POST /forks — no curl in image); (3) allowlist: patch warren-secrets/warren-public-allowlist + rollout restart warren, then warren add-project; (4) overlay config: policy.json (mutations flipped) + grammar.json + manifest.json + summaries.json {}; compute manifest digest by running validateCampaignManifest and reading the mismatch error; (5) apply -k, wait ~60s configmap mount propagation (grep the mounted file), exec manifest import + approve --by jayminwest, set CAMPAIGN_ID env, apply; (6) post-run: verify fork compare, STRIP harness artifacts (warren-194a), write summaries.json keyed by issue, apply, next tick renders pr_intent + pr_execute. Gotchas: amendments CANNOT change provider/model — re-import a higher campaignVersion (invalidates prior); approvedAt must not be in the future; provider keys live in warren-runs namespace as warren-<provider>-key/api-key.

Duplicate dispatch: seeds issue warren-2ec3 produced two warren runs and two PRs (#1158 and #1161) implementing the same classifier. #1161 merged first and follow-up work built on it; #1158 sat conflicting for days. When a PR's 'conflicts' are files added-in-both, check whether the same seeds issue already merged via another run before attempting a rebase — a tip-to-tip diff (git diff main branch -- <dir>) shows whether main is strictly ahead.
resolution: Closed #1158 as superseded with an explanatory comment and deleted its branch; main confirmed strictly ahead (had the merged classifier plus ~2k lines of follow-up work).

name: parallel-multi-campaign-ticks
description: Running N campaigns in parallel on one controller pod (2026-09-01 pilots, 3 campaigns): the daemon ticks only $CAMPAIGN_ID and pr_intent reads the repository policy from the MOUNTED CAMPAIGN_POLICY_PATH (not the DB), failing closed with policy_upstream_mismatch when another campaign's policy is mounted. Working recipe: kubectl cp each campaign's policy.json+grammar.json to the PVC (/app/data/campaign-files/<name>-*.json), then exec ticks with env overrides: sh -c 'CAMPAIGN_POLICY_PATH=... CAMPAIGN_BOT_GRAMMAR_PATH=... bun run src/cli/main.ts tick --campaign <cc-id> --grammar <path>'. Summaries stay in one merged mounted summaries.json keyed by issue number (distinct issue numbers across campaigns collide-free). Import still needs the campaign's manifest+policy mounted via configmap swap (~30-80s propagation each); imports are sequential, ticks are parallel. Filed warren-fe5d for the proper fix.

Target-selection misread: the fastembed #689 'maintainer engaged on fix options' signal was actually a fellow CONTRIBUTOR (denis-samatov) asking maintainers to choose a scope and offering to implement — the issue was design-gated AND socially claimed. Caught only on close re-read of the comment before dispatch; swapped the pilot to sqlfmt #548 (maintainer-acknowledged, direction stated).
resolution: Before picking a campaign issue from a scout report, verify the engaged commenter's author_association (MEMBER/OWNER vs CONTRIBUTOR/NONE) and whether their comment claims implementation intent; a contributor proposing options gates the issue on a maintainer decision and makes racing them bad etiquette and bad odds.

name: pilot-campaign-empirics-2026-09-01
description: 3-repo parallel pilot (goal: first merged external PR): mozilla-ai/any-llm#1365 (issue 1359, run $0.09, 2 files +106/-6, ~6min), vitest-dev/eslint-plugin-vitest#963 (issue 939, $0.57, 3 files +83/-2, zero artifacts committed), tconbeer/sqlfmt#873 (issue 548, $1.52, 8 files +415/-9, new dialect following ClickHouse wiring). Total agent spend $2.18 for 3 upstream PRs, ~90min wall-clock zero-to-3-PRs including fork/allowlist/register/import/approve. Target-selection basis: 4-agent scout fan-out measuring external-PR merge medians (any-llm 1.0d 27/30 external, eslint-plugin-vitest ~20h 27/30, sqlfmt ~3-4d solo-maintainer 2-PR queue). Hard blocklist found: wemake-services + Astral repos (written autonomous-agent ban), firecrawl (insider-only velocity). Reap opens a fork-internal PR per run — close it after the controller's cross-fork PR exists (closed #1 on all three forks).

A merged campaign-controller fix does not reach the cluster on merge: deploy-gke.yml workflow_dispatch defaults deploy=false and only the release path rolls forward, so PR #1187 (non-draft PRs) sat unrolled on the 04:30 build and three pilot PRs opened as drafts at 17:40. The 17:19 deploy then failed at Apply overlay (RBAC) and skipped the controller roll step.
resolution: Check the live tag with kubectl -n warren get deploy campaign-controller; run gh workflow run deploy-gke.yml --ref main -f deploy=true when a controller change must go live before the next release; mark already-opened drafts ready with the warren-secrets bot token.

name: bot-token-location
description: The warren-run-bot PAT with repo+workflow scope lives in warren-secrets/github-token; the live campaign-controller Deployment reads that key. campaign-controller-secrets/github-token is the old notifications-only PAT and cannot mark PRs ready or update branches. Operator actions on bot-authored PRs (gh pr ready, PUT repos/O/R/pulls/N/update-branch) use GH_TOKEN pulled from warren-secrets.

warren-194a recurred on the openclaw #132081 follow-up run (run_gevytzavaht0, pi/claude-sonnet-4-5): despite an explicit prompt rule never to stage .pi/ or .warren/, the agent committed the merge with git add -A and swept .warren/agent.json into the contribution branch. Prompt instructions do not hold under a merge-conflict workflow; the fix has to be structural (workspace-level exclude or reap-time strip).
resolution: Removed the file with a DELETE to the Contents API on the fork branch using the warren-secrets bot token (commit 203fa6f6); no clone needed. Audit every warren-pushed branch for .warren/agent.json before treating it as review-ready.

name: campaign-controller golden refresh flow
description: Golden refresh for extensions/campaign-controller PR-body templates: run WARREN_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 bun test src/pr-intent/intender.test.ts for the three intent goldens; the body-refresh golden has the same WARREN_UPDATE_GOLDENS branch in src/pr-execute/body-refresh.test.ts (round-trip re-read after write, preserves the contract/baseFacts/refresh/refreshedFacts keys via {...GOLDEN, body}).
